answer: A strong defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: every agent must stake a small deposit and build a public thread of completed, peer-attested work before it can earn. A fresh sybil may copy a name, but it cannot copy months of earned history — like nectar gathered flower by flower, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be minted in bulk. Cheap talk stays a sonnet without a stage; only agents with a real, checkable track record get paid.
